sections.html:
Bluffton is a town in southern Beaufort County, mainly along US 278 between Hilton Head Island and Interstate 95. It is part of the Hilton Head Island metropolitan area, though Jasper County, which shares that area, does not contain the town.

The town covers 54.19 square miles, of which 51.97 are land, which makes it the fifth-largest municipality in South Carolina by land area. The 2020 census counted 27,716 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 36,807. The May River runs through the center of town and the New River forms its southwest boundary.

For a seller, the layout has a quirk. Strict state annexation laws left unincorporated pockets, called doughnut holes, inside the town limits. A house with a Bluffton address may therefore sit under county rules and not town rules, so check which applies before you assume anything about permits or rental licenses.

Bluffton was settled in 1728 and incorporated in 1852. The original one-square-mile core, now called Old Town, sits on a bluff above the May River, on land once home to the Yamasee.

The Bluffton Movement of 1844 protested federal taxes and is tied to the early secession push in South Carolina. On June 4, 1863, Union forces destroyed about two-thirds of the town's roughly 60 structures. Old Town was named a National Historic District in 1996, and the Heyward House became the town's welcome center in 2000.

Bluffton Oyster Company opened in 1899, and galleries line Calhoun Street today.

sections.h2: How fast has Bluffton grown, and what does that mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Very fast. Bluffton's population grew 882.7 percent from 2000 to 2010 and another 121.2 percent from 2010 to 2020. Planned developments from the early 2000s housing boom drove much of it, and the Sun City Hilton Head community and 1990s growth on Hilton Head Island had already revived commercial activity in town.

Several of those developments stayed partly unfinished after the Great Recession. That history means a Bluffton house can sit in a community with a homeowners association, a master plan or amenities still under development.

  • Ask the association for its governing documents and any unpaid dues before you sign a contract.
  • Check whether your lot is inside the town limits or in a doughnut hole.
  • Collect any plat, survey and permit records you have, since the county's recording rules ask for a legal description or a reference to a recorded plat.

Bluffton's median age was 40.5 in the 2020 census, and tourism and higher education are both part of the economy.

sections.h2: How do hurricanes and flooding affect a Bluffton house?
sections.html:
Bluffton is in South Carolina's Southern Coastal Hurricane Region, and Beaufort County has a single evacuation zone, so an evacuation order applies to the whole county. The Bluffton Township Fire District, at (843) 757-2800, points residents to the state's official zone maps at Hurricane.SC and a town evacuation routes PDF.

The climate is humid subtropical, with mild winters and hot, humid summers. August is the wettest month, and the yearly total is about 50.4 inches. Buyers in a coastal county reasonably ask about wind and water, so it helps to gather the roof age, past claims and any flood paperwork you have.

The elevation is only about 20 feet.

sections.h2: Do Bluffton's short-term rental rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
They can, if the house is used as a rental. Town Ordinance 2023-248, adopted May 15, 2023, regulates short-term rentals, which it defines as renting a residential dwelling for fewer than 30 days.

  • Operating a short-term rental business requires a license from the Town Clerk, unless an exemption is granted.
  • A license runs one calendar year and must be posted where it can be seen at the property.
  • The clerk can suspend, revoke or decline to renew a license for good cause.
  • A person affected can appeal to the Town Manager within 10 days of written notice, and then to Town Council within 10 days. The council's decision is final.

A buyer of a rental will ask whether the license is current and whether the home sits inside the town.

sections.h2: How does property tax work for a Bluffton seller?
sections.html:
Beaufort County reassessed in 2023 and its next reassessment is scheduled for 2028. State law requires a reassessment every five years.

A primary residence is assessed at 4 percent of appraised value if the owner applied, and other residential and commercial property at 6 percent. The county's Important Dates page gives January 1 through January 15 of the following year for the 4 percent application, and the same window for an objection to value, or within 90 days of an assessment notice. You cannot use both options in one tax year.

A sale is an assessable transfer of interest. The appraisal date is December 31 of the year of transfer, and the new value applies for the following tax year. The county's transfer exemption can reduce the market value by up to 25 percent, but not below the current county record, and the application is due before January 31. Questions go to the Assessor at (843) 255-2400.

Tax is payable through January 15, with state penalties of 3 percent from January 16, another 7 percent after the second of February and another 5 percent after March 17.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Beaufort County involve?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the Beaufort County Register of Deeds, 100 Ribaut Road in Beaufort, open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. The phone is (843) 255-2555.

The county's checklist is detailed. A deed generally needs a return-to name and address, two witnesses who are not parties to the deal, a notary block, a legal description, the grantee's address, a district, map and parcel number and a derivation clause. Warranty deeds also need a preparation clause.

The county lists a flat $15 deed fee plus the state and county fee of $1.85 per $500 of the price, as of August 1, 2019. Hilton Head Island has an extra transfer fee, and it applies only to certain district numbers. Three e-recording companies are accepted, and documents received after 4:30 p.m. are processed the next business day.

South Carolina requires an attorney to supervise the closing. Ask them to confirm the current fees.

faqs.q: Is Bluffton, SC in Beaufort County or Jasper County?
faqs.a: Beaufort County. Jasper County is part of the same metropolitan area but does not contain the town of Bluffton.

faqs.q: Does Bluffton require a license to rent a house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. Town Ordinance 2023-248 requires a short-term rental license from the Town Clerk for rentals of fewer than 30 days, unless an exemption is granted. Licenses run for one calendar year.

faqs.q: When is Beaufort County's next reassessment?
faqs.a: The county says 2028, after its last reassessment in 2023. State law requires one every five years.

faqs.q: Does a sale raise the property tax on a Bluffton house?
faqs.a: It can. A sale is an assessable transfer of interest, so the home is reappraised as of December 31 of that year. The new value applies the next tax year, and a transfer exemption may reduce it by up to 25 percent.

faqs.q: Does Beaufort County evacuate by zone?
faqs.a: No. The county has a single evacuation zone, so an order covers the whole county.
